findings.description: The invite code is the only secret that grants workspace membership, but `random.choices` uses the Mersenne Twister, which is predictable. An attacker who observes a few codes could recover the generator state and predict codes for other links, joining workspaces uninvited.
findings.suggestion: Use the `secrets` module, e.g. `"".join(secrets.choice(CODE_ALPHABET) for _ in range(CODE_LENGTH))`.
findings.title: Invite codes generated with non-cryptographic PRNG

findings.description: `accept` checks only `revoked` and `uses >= max_uses`, but not `now < expires_at`. Expired links can therefore still be used to join a workspace, so the TTL is never enforced. `is_active(now)` already covers all three conditions.
findings.title: accept() does not check link expiry

findings.description: `uses` is checked, then `directory.add` is called, and only afterwards is `uses` incremented, with no locking. Concurrent accepts of a single-use link can all pass the check and all join, so `max_uses` is exceeded. The shared dict and counter are also unsynchronised.
findings.suggestion: Guard accept with a lock, or reserve a use (increment) atomically before adding the member and roll back on failure.
findings.title: Check-then-act on uses allows exceeding max_uses
